name: Synthetic Short Call
summary: 100 short shares plus one short put at the same strike replicates a naked short call; unlimited upside risk plus borrow risk, and a structure with essentially no retail use case.

legs.strike_rule: Strike at or below spot, put delta -0.30 to -0.50

max_profit: (entry_spot - put_strike) x 100 + put_credit, capped at the put strike
max_loss: UNDEFINED (unlimited) — the short shares lose without limit as the underlying rises and the short put provides only the premium as offset
when_to_use: There is no good retail use case. It is the mirror of a covered call but the 'cover' is a short stock position, which is not capital-efficient, incurs borrow fees, owes dividends, and carries buy-in risk. Listed here for completeness of the family.
entry_rules: PERMANENT DENYLIST RECOMMENDATION. The short put is not covered by short stock in the sense Alpaca's Level 3 coverage rule requires, so the multi-leg order is rejected; and the combined position has unbounded loss. Requires Level 4 plus short-stock capability.
Even at Level 4 the structure should be rejected by the risk layer: unbounded loss on a $50k account with a share-settled American underlying.

Documented here so the strategy classifier can recognise it and refuse it if a leg combination accidentally produces it (e.g. a covered call whose shares were sold, leaving a naked call, is the same exposure by a different route).
management_rules: If the classifier ever detects this exposure in the live book (short shares plus short put, or any naked short call equivalent), raise a critical alert and flatten both legs in the same session, options leg first.
No profit target or stop is specified because the position should not exist.
exit_rules: MANDATORY: close the short put no later than 15:40 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
If spot < put_strike at any time on expiration day, close the short put by 14:00 ET — assignment would buy 100 shares, covering the short, which is an uncontrolled unwind at the strike.
Close the short shares before any ex-dividend date; the short owes the full dividend.
assignment_risk: On the short put, which is assigned when ITM with extrinsic below ~$0.05. Assignment buys 100 shares at the strike and closes out the short stock automatically — a forced unwind at a price the system did not choose. Plus borrow buy-in risk on the share leg at any time.
buying_power: Reg T short stock margin (50% of proceeds) plus naked short put margin, netted by the broker to roughly the short stock requirement. About $5,000+ per unit on a $100 name.
common_mistakes: Reaching this exposure accidentally, by selling the shares out from under a covered call or by having a long stock leg assigned away. The position monitor must check for it explicitly every cycle.
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
